extracted.intended_audience: students enrolled in (or considering) MIT OpenCourseWare 'Introduction to Partial Differential Equations' course
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus for an application-motivated introductory course on partial differential equations, specifying prerequisites, homework/exam policies, grading, collaboration and citation expectations. Targets how students should prepare, submit, and how work will be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must have completed 18.100 Analysis and one of 18.06 Linear Algebra, 18.700 Linear Algebra, or 18.701 Algebra I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These courses are required to ensure readiness for the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homework frequency and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be an assignment almost every week; homework assignments will typically be posted on the course website on Thursday and due at the start of class on the following Thursday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homework is the primary regular coursework mechanism; plan to check the site weekly and meet the Thursday deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: No late assignments policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No late assignments will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict deadline policy — late submissions are not allowed under any circumstance (as stated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lowest homework score policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Your lowest homework score will not factor into your grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One low homework score is dropped when computing course grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homework grading criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Your homework will be graded both on correctness and on the quality of your written arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions must not only get the right answer but present clear, well-reasoned, and well-written arguments; presentation matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format (LaTeX encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: For your own benefit, you are encouraged to learn how to use LaTeX to type up your homework; however, you can turn in neatly handwritten assignments if you prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX is recommended for clarity and professionalism, but neat handwriting is acceptable — choose whichever yields clear exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration is encouraged: 'work with your classmates' meaning every member of a collaborative effort is expected to be an active contributor. The version you turn in must be written in your own words and your own writing style, and you must fully understand the written arguments; copying someone else’s homework line by line is plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you collaborate, list the names of the people you worked with at the top of the assignment. Collaboration must be substantive (active contribution) and must not involve verbatim copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use a resource (e.g. Wikipedia, a textbook, a journal article, etc.), you must cite it using one of the standard citation styles. Indicate the title, author, volume number, year, and page number (or web address if appropriate) of your references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever external resources inform your solution, provide a proper bibliographic citation so sources are clear and traceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exam format and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a single 90 minute midterm exam held in class. Both the midterm and the final will be closed book, closed notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Midterm is 90 minutes; no homework due that week. Final exam is cumulative with a slight emphasis on material covered after the midterm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Final grade composition: Homework 30%, Midterm Exam 30%, Final Exam 40%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates relative weight of course components; homework collectively accounts for 30% (with one drop), exams 70%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role/importance of homework
rubrics_metrics.description: Homework is perhaps the most important component of this course: it provides you with regular feedback on whether or not you are keeping up with the material, and it challenges you to creatively apply what you have already learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should treat homework as the primary vehicle for learning and feedback rather than a purely summative exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course meeting logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Course meets 2 sessions per week, 1.5 hours per session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance and participation during these scheduled sessions are implied as the primary in-person instruction times.
